difficultyReason: Single causal claim: hospital implemented new antiseptic protocol → infection rates fell. Correct answer provides obvious alternative explanation (antibiotic availability).
stimulus: A hospital implemented a new antiseptic protocol for surgical instruments last January. Since then, surgical site infections have dropped by 40%. Hospital administrators conclude that the new protocol caused the reduction in infections.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hospital's infection rates had been rising steadily for three years before the protocol was implemented.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An effective new antibiotic that combats surgical infections became widely available in the region exactly one month before the protocol was introduced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital increased its nursing staff by 15 percent during the same period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Surgeons at the hospital had received training in the new protocol one month before its official implementation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Other hospitals in the region have not experienced similar decreases in infection rates.

explanations.correct: By introducing a competing cause (the new antibiotic) that also became available in the same timeframe, this answer weakens the claim that the protocol caused the reduction. The infection drop may have been due to the antibiotic, not the protocol.
explanations.A: Consistent with the protocol's effectiveness but does not weaken the causal claim.
explanations.C: While plausible as an alternative cause, does not weaken as directly as the antibiotic, which specifically targets the mechanism causing surgical infections.
explanations.D: Supports the protocol's implementation and thus strengthens the argument slightly.
explanations.E: Raises doubt about generalizability but does not undermine the causal claim at this hospital.

difficultyReason: Direct causal inference: company switched to remote work → productivity rose by 20%. Correct answer offers an obvious alternative explanation (new project launch).
stimulus: After implementing a company-wide remote work policy last March, a technology firm measured a 20 percent increase in employee productivity. The firm's management concludes that remote work itself has boosted productivity.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A majority of the company's employees expressed preference for remote work arrangements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company had conducted a pilot remote work program with 30 employees the year prior, which also showed productivity gains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A lucrative new client contract requiring significant additional work began in April, just one month after the remote work policy was adopted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Employee morale at the company had been declining before the remote work policy was introduced.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Employees working remotely reported higher job satisfaction than those in the office.

explanations.correct: By introducing an alternative cause (the new client contract requiring more work) that also occurred in the same period, this choice weakens the causal inference. The productivity boost may have resulted from increased workload, not remote work.
explanations.A: Shows remote work was desired but does not explain the productivity increase.
explanations.B: Actually strengthens the argument by showing remote work has a track record of improving productivity.
explanations.D: Irrelevant to the productivity measurement; morale and output are distinct.
explanations.E: Consistent with remote work being beneficial but not an alternative cause for productivity gains.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim: banning plastic bags → litter decreased. Correct answer provides alternative explanation (crackdown on littering itself).
stimulus: A city enacted a ban on single-use plastic bags in all retail stores. Three months later, researchers measured a 25 percent reduction in plastic litter on city streets. Environmental officials claim that the plastic bag ban caused this decrease in litter.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city had been accumulating plastic litter for years before implementing the ban.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simultaneously with the plastic bag ban, the city launched an aggressive public awareness campaign against littering and increased fines for littering violations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reusable bags recommended as alternatives to plastic bags are more durable and less likely to tear.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The city's parks and recreation department had already been increasing street cleanup efforts over the previous two years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Studies from other cities show that plastic bag bans reduce plastic waste in landfills but not on city streets.

explanations.correct: This introduces a direct competing cause (the anti-littering campaign and increased fines) that coincided exactly with the ban. The litter reduction may be due to enforcement and public awareness, not the bag ban itself.
explanations.A: Background information that does not undermine the causal link.
explanations.C: Describes a property of reusable bags; irrelevant to why litter decreased.
explanations.D: Pre-dates the ban and does not explain the recent decrease.
explanations.E: Raises doubts about generalizability but does not undermine the causal reasoning for this particular city.

difficultyReason: Causal claim: new curriculum → test scores rose. Correct answer offers confounding variable (demographic shift in student population).
stimulus: A school district implemented a revised mathematics curriculum emphasizing conceptual understanding. One year later, standardized math test scores at district schools rose by 12 percent on average. District officials attribute the improvement directly to the new curriculum.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Teachers reported that the new curriculum required significantly more preparation time than the previous curriculum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Math test scores had been falling for five consecutive years before the new curriculum was adopted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: During the same year, the school district began an aggressive program to recruit top performers from neighboring districts, fundamentally changing the demographic composition of the student body.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The revised curriculum aligns closely with mathematics standards adopted by most other states.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several parents expressed concerns about the transition to a conceptual approach in mathematics.

explanations.correct: By introducing a confounding factor (recruitment of top-performing students), this choice weakens the claim that the curriculum caused the score improvement. The higher scores may result from a more capable student population, not the curriculum itself.
explanations.A: Concerns workload but does not explain score gains.
explanations.B: Background information; actually supports curriculum change as a reversal factor.
explanations.D: Supports curriculum quality but does not undermine the causal attribution.
explanations.E: Reflects opinion but does not explain the score gains.

difficultyReason: Single causal argument: social media reduction → sleep improved. Correct answer offers alternative cause (seasonal change).
stimulus: A sleep researcher conducted a study in which participants reduced their social media use by an average of three hours daily for three months. By the end of the study period, participants reported significantly better sleep quality and longer average sleep duration. The researcher concludes that excessive social media use impairs sleep and that reducing it improves sleep quality.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sleep quality varies significantly among individuals based on genetic factors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The study period coincided with the transition from autumn to winter, when the duration of daylight decreases significantly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some participants in the study had never had social media accounts to begin with.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Participants in the study were fully aware that the study aimed to measure the effects of social media reduction on sleep.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Social media platforms have become increasingly important for professional networking.

explanations.correct: By identifying an alternative cause (decreased daylight in winter, which naturally improves sleep), this weakens the inference that social media reduction caused the improvement. The seasonal change may be responsible.
explanations.A: Acknowledges variation but does not undermine the causal link.
explanations.C: Raises a study design issue but does not provide an alternative cause.
explanations.D: Introduces potential placebo effect but is more about study design than causation.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim: mandatory employee training → customer satisfaction rose. Correct answer provides competing cause (pricing change).
stimulus: A retail corporation implemented mandatory customer service training for all employees. Two months after the training was completed, customer satisfaction scores increased by 18 percent. Company executives conclude that the training program directly caused the improvement in customer satisfaction.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The customer service training was developed by an external consulting firm specializing in retail customer experience.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the same time as the training rollout, the company reduced prices on its most popular product lines by an average of 10 percent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Customer satisfaction surveys were conducted more frequently after the training than they had been before.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many employees had received informal customer service coaching prior to the mandatory training program.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Competitors of the corporation have not implemented similar customer service training programs.

explanations.correct: By introducing a competing cause (price reduction), this choice weakens the causal attribution. Customers may be more satisfied due to lower prices rather than improved service from training.
explanations.A: Supports training quality; does not weaken causation.
explanations.C: Relates to survey methodology but does not explain the actual satisfaction increase.
explanations.D: Prior coaching might support the training's benefit; does not undermine it.
explanations.E: Irrelevant to whether training caused the satisfaction increase at this company.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal inference: website redesign → sales increased. Correct answer offers alternative explanation (seasonal sales patterns).
stimulus: An e-commerce company redesigned its website with a focus on simplifying the checkout process. In the month following the redesign launch, online sales rose by 22 percent compared to the same month the previous year. Management attributes the sales increase to the new website design.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The previous website design had been in use for over ten years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The month in question is November, which is part of the holiday shopping season when online sales typically increase significantly compared to the previous year regardless of website changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Customers who used the new checkout process reported that it was easier to navigate than the previous design.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The company had not advertised the website redesign to its existing customer base.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some customers expressed difficulty adapting to the new website layout.

explanations.correct: By attributing the sales increase to a seasonal pattern (holiday shopping), this undermines the claim that the redesign caused the increase. The boost may be typical for November regardless of website changes.
explanations.A: Background information; does not undermine causation.
explanations.C: Supports the redesign's effectiveness; does not weaken the causal claim.
explanations.D: Lack of promotion might explain lower-than-expected gains but does not undermine what was actually observed.
explanations.E: Some adaptation issues do not negate the overall sales increase or its cause.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim: stricter building codes → injury rates fell. Correct answer provides alternative explanation (increased safety awareness).
stimulus: A city adopted stricter building safety codes for commercial establishments. Within one year of the codes' implementation, workplace injuries in the city's commercial sector fell by 30 percent. City officials conclude that the stricter building codes caused this reduction in injuries.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new building codes addressed multiple safety hazards identified in previous injury reports.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Commercial establishments had to invest substantially in renovations to comply with the new codes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coinciding with the adoption of the new building codes, state regulators also launched an aggressive workplace safety inspection program and issued substantial fines for violations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Workplace injuries in neighboring cities without the new codes remained unchanged over the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Many workers expressed concerns about understanding the new building code requirements.

explanations.correct: By introducing a competing cause (state inspection program and fines), this weakens the attribution to building codes alone. The injury reduction may result from increased compliance pressure and safety enforcement, not the codes themselves.
explanations.A: Shows codes address real hazards; supports the causal claim.
explanations.B: Indicates codes were taken seriously but does not explain injury reduction.
explanations.D: Shows a contrast but does not identify an alternative cause for the decrease.
explanations.E: Concerns about understanding do not explain why injuries actually decreased.

difficultyReason: Direct causal claim: free breakfast program → student attendance improved. Correct answer offers confounding factor (increased parent involvement).
stimulus: A school district initiated a free breakfast program for all students in low-income neighborhoods. The following academic year, student attendance in these schools increased by 17 percent. District officials conclude that the free breakfast program was responsible for the attendance improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Research studies have shown that eating breakfast can improve student attention and academic performance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attendance rates had been declining in these schools for three consecutive years before the breakfast program was launched.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the same time as the breakfast program began, a community coalition successfully organized an intensive parent engagement campaign encouraging families to prioritize school attendance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some students in the district have access to meals at home before school.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The breakfast program included nutritionally balanced options meeting federal dietary standards.

explanations.correct: By introducing a competing cause (parent engagement campaign), this weakens the claim that the breakfast program caused the attendance increase. The improvement may result from increased family involvement rather than the program itself.
explanations.A: Shows breakfast benefits cognition but does not explain attendance specifically.
explanations.B: Background showing prior decline supports breakfast program as a reversal; does not weaken.
explanations.D: Acknowledges variation but does not explain the attendance increase.
explanations.E: Supports program quality but does not undermine causal attribution.

difficultyReason: Simple causal argument: new library hours → circulation increased. Correct answer provides alternative explanation (new collection addition).
stimulus: A public library extended its operating hours to stay open until 10 p.m. on weeknights, an increase from the previous 6 p.m. closing time. Three months after the extended hours took effect, the library reported that book circulation had increased by 35 percent compared to the same three-month period the previous year. Library management concludes that the extended hours directly caused the increase in circulation.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The library spent substantial funds on staffing necessary to maintain the extended hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the same period, the library added 10,000 new volumes to its collection, representing a 25 percent increase in total holdings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patrons who use the library primarily during evening hours reported high satisfaction with the extended hours.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The library's loan period for books remained unchanged at four weeks.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some library staff expressed concerns about fatigue from working additional evening shifts.

explanations.correct: By introducing an alternative cause (the substantial addition of new books), this weakens the inference that extended hours caused the circulation increase. More books available naturally leads to more circulation, regardless of hours.
explanations.A: Describes a cost but does not provide an alternative cause.
explanations.C: Shows extended hours were appreciated but does not explain circulation figures.
explanations.D: Loan period unchanged means this variable did not confound; does not weaken.
explanations.E: Staff concerns are irrelevant to circulation measurement.
